questions.title: Which Chinese province will evacuate the most people in preparation for Typhoon Bavi by July 11, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Chinese authorities' figures in contemporaneous news coverage. Resolve to the Chinese province with the largest reported number of people evacuated in preparation for Typhoon Bavi as of July 11, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-11 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the province's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Significant July 5 westward shift in physical meteorological guidance reverses part of July 4's northward swing and sharply boosts Fujian's evacuation outlook by July 11. As Super Typhoon Bavi (CMA 20:00 CST July 5: 62 m/s, 13.2N 146.8E; CWA 910 hPa, 320-350 km gale radius) batters Rota/Guam as a Cat 5 storm, July 5 ECMWF deterministic guidance shifted westward ('路徑西修', ETtoday/TVBS/LTN) under a deeper northern subtropical ridge on July 10 to project direct landfall in Yilan-Hualien (eastern/northeastern Taiwan) early July 11, with NCEP GFS likewise extending the ridge westward (Lin De-en, EBC) and AI models—while still recurving earlier toward China/Korea—also trending westward ('仍西修中'). CMA/China Weather Network chief meteorologist Xin Xin (July 5 22:05 CST) explicitly frames two primary mainland branches: bypassing north of Taiwan straight into Zhejiang if the July 7-8 westerly trough weakens the ridge slightly, versus hitting Taiwan first and then making landfall in Fujian if the ridge stays strong. Crucially for the July 11 evacuation cutoff, Fujian Meteorological Bureau held an urgent July 5 15:00 CST special consultation—three days earlier than normal—forecasting Bavi enters Fujian's typhoon warning zone afternoon-night of July 9 (8-10 Beaufort coastal winds, outer rainbands hitting Fuzhou July 10). Updating our 4-regime model raises Fujian +0.080 (0.28 -> 0.36), trims Zhejiang -0.050 (0.56 -> 0.51, still favored across north-of-Taiwan/Zhejiang direct tracks and early East China Sea recurvatures), cuts Guangdong -0.020 (0.06 -> 0.04 as Bashi Channel tracks disappear from official briefings), and holds Shanghai (0.055) and Jiangsu (0.025) with 1% residual.

local_articles.title: Super typhoon Bavi spares Philippines, heads for Taiwan with 300 kph winds
local_articles.snippet: Weather authorities declared a low chance of super-typhoon Bavi making landfall in the Philippines as it barrels westward from the Mariana Islands in the Pacific. With gusts of up to 300 kilometers per hour (km/h), 2026’s second super typhoon will enter the Philippine area of responsibility(PAR) on Tuesday but will curve northwards towards Taiwan. This is the second time this year that a freak weather event is sparing the Philippines and hitting its neighbors Taiwan and Japan. A super typhoon is the most powerful category of tropical cyclone in the Northwestern Pacific Ocean, defined by maximum sustained surface winds of 185 km/h (115 mph) or greater—the equivalent of a strong Category 4 or Category 5 hurricane. questions.title: If Bavi makes landfall in mainland China during July 2026, which province will it strike first?
questions.background: Landfall occurs when a tropical cyclone's center crosses the coastline. This question concerns only mainland China.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official landfall reports from China’s National Meteorological Center, supplemented by contemporaneous reporting from major news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the province containing the location of Bavi’s first mainland-China landfall during July 2026. Subsequent landfalls do not count. If no qualifying landfall occurs during that month, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: July 5 westward track shift in ECMWF (now projecting direct Yilan-Hualien Taiwan landfall early July 11 under a stronger northern subtropical ridge, ETtoday/TVBS/LTN), westward ridge extension in NCEP GFS (Lin De-en, EBC), westward drift in AI models ('仍西修中'), and Fujian Meteorological Bureau's urgent July 5 special consultation (projecting entry into Fujian's warning zone July 9 and citing ~60% historical Fujian landfall rate for early-July super typhoons entering the zone) restore a clear Fujian lead over Zhejiang conditional on a mainland China landfall. CMA chief meteorologist Xin Xin (July 5 22:05 CST) frames the core mainland bifurcation as either bypassing north of Taiwan straight into Zhejiang or striking Taiwan first and then landing in Fujian, while Bashi Channel/Guangdong tracks have disappeared from official briefings. Because Q66613 is strictly conditional on a qualifying mainland China landfall (void if Bavi recurves cleanly to Korea/Japan), Bayes' rule weights the elevated Taiwan-landfall->Fujian regime (~92% mainland landfall) far more heavily than AI early-recurvature tracks (~25% mainland landfall), lifting Fujian +0.055 (0.405 -> 0.46), trimming Zhejiang -0.015 (0.395 -> 0.38), cutting Guangdong -0.025 (0.08 -> 0.055), and holding Shanghai (0.05) and Jiangsu (0.035) with 2% residual for Shandong/Liaoning/other.

local_articles.title: Super Typhoon Bavi Makes Landfall In US Pacific Island, Residents Warned To Stay Indoors
local_articles.snippet: Super Typhoon Bavi made landfall Monday over a tiny US territorial island in the western Pacific near Guam, bringing powerful winds and torrential rain to the Northern Mariana Islands as residents were urged to stay indoors. The storm started passing through the island of Rota Monday morning local time, according to the National Weather Service. The typhoon threatened other parts of the Northern Mariana Islands, a US territory east of the Philippines, as well as Guam. The area was still recovering from another destructive cyclone earlier this year. On the island of Saipan, the international airport recorded wind gusts of more than 100 mph (161 kph), weather service meteorologist Marcus Landon Aydlett said.
